# SRS: Elite-Fresh Space Trading Game

Status: draft

## 1. Introduction

This System Requirements Specification defines the HOW contract for Elite-Fresh, a single-player Elite-inspired space trading and combat game delivered as a browser-based single-page application. The SRS is derived from the accepted PRD (artifact id 2) and decomposes the frozen acceptance baseline (23 accepted ACs) into modules, invariants, file surfaces, and test strategies.

## 2. Architecture

### 2.1 Architectural Style

**Style:** Modular monolith (client-side) with a thin static-file server.

**Rationale:** The complexity profile is XS with sequential topology and no shared mutation risk. Game state is owned by a single browser session. The server is a static file server with one health endpoint; all game logic runs client-side in a single browser tab. Hexagonal, ports-and-adapters, or clean architecture would add structural overhead with no concurrency or deployment boundary to justify it. The modular monolith exposes stable module seams and clear ownership while staying minimal.

### 2.2 Module Manifest

| Module | Responsibility | Owned Surfaces |
|---|---|---|
| server | Static file serving, /healthz endpoint, one-command startup | `server/index.ts`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` |
| galaxy | Star system data, galaxy map rendering | `src/galaxy.ts` |
| trading | Commodity market, buy/sell logic, per-system pricing | `src/trading.ts` |
| travel | Hyperspace jump execution, fuel consumption | `src/travel.ts` |
| combat | Ship-to-ship combat, pirate encounter trigger, pirate AI, flee logic | `src/combat.ts` |
| upgrades | Ship upgrade purchases and stat application | `src/upgrades.ts` |
| save-load | Game state serialization and deserialization, persistence | `src/save-load.ts` |
| game-state | Central player state: credits, cargo, ship stats, position, rating | `src/game-state.ts` |
| rating | Elite rating calculation and tier progression | `src/rating.ts` |
| rendering | Canvas rendering, visual effects (parallax, hyperspace, lasers), HUD | `src/rendering.ts`, `src/ui.ts` |

### 2.3 Port Registry

The sequential XS topology has no shared or concurrent module boundaries requiring formal port contracts. The only deployment boundary is the server/client HTTP interface, documented below.

| Port | Provider | Consumer | Protocol | Direction | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| StaticAssetServer | server | Chrome browser | HTTP (static files) | server -> client | Serves `public/` directory; no API calls from client to server |
| HealthEndpoint | server | Factory verification | HTTP GET /healthz | server responds | Returns `{ status: "healthy" }`; no auth required, local-only |

No inter-module ports are defined. Client modules communicate through direct TypeScript function calls within the same browser runtime.

### 2.4 Invariant Registry

| ID | Predicate | Check Layer | Provider |
|---|---|---|---|
| INV-1 | `fuel >= 0` at all times | L1 (unit) | jest |
| INV-2 | `credits >= 0` after any transaction | L1 (unit) | jest |
| INV-3 | `cargo_count <= cargo_capacity` at all times | L1 (unit) | jest |
| INV-4 | `load(save(state)) == state` (save-restore identity) | L1 (unit) | jest |
| INV-5 | New game: `credits == 100`, `cargo_capacity == small`, `location == station` | L1 (unit) | jest |
| INV-6 | `exists commodity C, systems A, B: price(C, A) != price(C, B)` | L1 (unit) | jest |
| INV-7 | `rating_tier` is monotonic non-decreasing when profit or kills increase | L3 (integration) | jest |
| INV-8 | `accumulated_profit >= 0` and `combat_kills >= 0` at all times | L1 (unit) | jest |
| INV-9 | `threshold(tier_N+1) >= threshold(tier_N)` for all rating tiers | L1 (unit) | jest |
| INV-10 | No outbound network requests to non-localhost hosts | L0 (smoke) | puppeteer |

## 3. Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| Star system | A named location in the galaxy containing one station |
| Station | A dockable location where the player can trade and buy upgrades |
| Commodity | A tradeable good with a per-system price |
| Hyperspace jump | Travel between star systems consuming fuel |
| Elite rating | A combat/trading rank progressing through defined tiers |
| HUD | Heads-up display showing ship status overlay during gameplay |
| Cargo capacity | Maximum number of commodity units the ship can carry |

## 4. Out of Scope

- Multi-player or networked gameplay.
- Deployment to any hosting environment.
- External CDN dependencies.
- Mobile or non-Chrome browser support.
- External API integrations.
- Persistence beyond the local browser (no server-side database).

## 5. Supporting Systems

- **Node.js runtime**: Required on the local machine to run the server.
- **Google Chrome**: The target browser for the client.
- **npm**: Package manager for dependency installation and script execution.

## 6. External Integrations

None. The game operates fully offline with no external service dependencies.

## 7. Security

The game runs locally with no user accounts, authentication, or sensitive data. Security axes:

| Axis | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Authentication | N/A | No user accounts; single-player local game |
| Authorization | N/A | No resource access control needed |
| Input validation | Applicable | Server validates /healthz is a GET request; client validates buy/sell/jump inputs (bounds checks covered by INV-1 through INV-3) |
| Data protection | N/A | No PII or sensitive data; save data is local browser state |
| Network security | N/A | No external network communication |

## 8. Technology Stack

| Component | Technology | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Server | TypeScript, Node.js, http module | Static file serving, /healthz |
| Client | TypeScript, HTML5 Canvas | Game rendering and logic |
| Build | tsc, bundled via single-command start | No separate build step |
| Test (L1) | Jest | Unit tests for game logic |
| Test (L0) | Puppeteer or custom Node script | Browser smoke test |
| Persistence | localStorage | Client-side save/load |

## 9. Runnable Stack Commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `npm install && npm start` | Install dependencies and start the game server |
| `npx jest` | Run all unit tests (L1, L3) |
| `npx jest --testPathPattern=smoke` | Run browser smoke test (L0) |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | Type-check all TypeScript sources |
| `npm run lint` | Lint all source files |

## 10. Test Strategy and Reachability

| Layer | Name | What it covers | Runner | Reachable modules |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L0 | Browser smoke test | Page loads, canvas renders, no external requests | Puppeteer / custom script | server, rendering |
| L1 | Unit tests | Trading math, jump/fuel logic, combat resolution, save/load round-trip, starting conditions, rating thresholds, price variation | jest | trading, travel, combat, save-load, game-state, rating, galaxy, upgrades |
| L2 | Performance benchmark | Frame rate measurement under load | Custom script | rendering |
| L3 | Integration tests | Save-restore identity, rating monotonicity across trade+combat sequences | jest | save-load, rating, trading, combat, game-state |

All client-side modules (galaxy, trading, travel, combat, upgrades, save-load, game-state, rating, rendering, ui) are reachable from Jest tests because they are pure TypeScript modules imported directly in Node.js. The server module is reachable via its exported HTTP handler.

## 11. Constraints

All constraints from the accepted brief are carried forward:

- **ord-c-001**: One-command startup (`npm install && npm start`) -> AC-22
- **ord-c-002**: No manual build steps -> AC-22
- **ord-c-003**: 60fps rendering on 2020 laptop in Chrome -> AC-20
- **ord-c-004**: TypeScript backend -> AC-22
- **ord-c-005**: Chrome client target -> AC-22
- **ord-c-006**: Local run required -> AC-22
- **ord-c-007**: Per-system price variation creating trade routes (deferred to development) -> AC-6
- **ord-c-008**: Ship upgrade cost balance (deferred to development) -> AC-13
- **ord-c-009**: Visual effects within 60fps budget (deferred to development) -> AC-7
- **ord-c-010**: Persistence mechanism selection (deferred to development) -> AC-15
- **ord-c-011**: Pirate AI behavior patterns (deferred to development) -> AC-10
- **ord-c-012**: No external CDN dependencies -> AC-22
- **ord-c-013**: Offline capability -> AC-22

## §12 Decision Log

| # | Decision | Source/profile | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Date |
|---|----------|----------------|-------------------------|-----------|------|
| 1 | Modular monolith with thin server | Complexity profile (XS, sequence, shared_mutation_risk=false) | Hexagonal, Clean architecture, Microservices | Sequential single-player game with no concurrent users or deployment boundaries. Modular monolith exposes seams without overhead. | 2026-08-25 |
| 2 | localStorage for persistence | Inherited from brief (deferred ord-c-010) | IndexedDB, File download/upload, In-memory only | Simplest mechanism for a single-player browser game; no server-side storage needed. | 2026-08-25 |
| 3 | Canvas (not WebGL) for rendering | PRD section 3.8, KISS for XS | WebGL, SVG, DOM-based | PRD lists Canvas first; 2D arcade game does not require GPU shaders. | 2026-08-25 |
| 4 | No inter-module port contracts | Sequential topology, no shared mutation | Event bus, DI container, Message passing | Direct function calls in a single runtime are sufficient. Ports add indirection with no concurrency boundary to protect. | 2026-08-25 |
| 5 | Jest for unit/integration testing | Inherited from brief (unit tests required) | Mocha+Chai, Vitest, Node assert | Jest is the most common TypeScript test runner; matches the one-command startup constraint. | 2026-08-25 |

## 13. D1 Canonical File/Module Surface

src/

  galaxy.ts             # Star system definitions, galaxy map data
  trading.ts            # buyCommodity, sellCommodity, getMarketForSystem
  travel.ts             # executeJump, canJump, fuelCost
  combat.ts             # CombatEngine, pirate AI states, resolveCombat, flee
  upgrades.ts           # purchaseUpgrade, getAvailableUpgrades, applyUpgrade
  save-load.ts          # saveGame, loadGame, hasSavedGame
  rating.ts             # calculateRating, RATING_TIERS, recordKill, recordProfit
  rendering.ts          # Canvas renderer, parallax starfield, hyperspace effect, laser VFX
  ui.ts                 # HUD overlay, screen management (map, station, combat)
public/
  index.html            # Single-page HTML shell
  style.css             # Minimal styles
tests/
  trading.test.ts       # AC-3, AC-4, AC-5, AC-6
  travel.test.ts        # AC-7, AC-8
  combat.test.ts        # AC-9, AC-10, AC-11, AC-12
  upgrades.test.ts      # AC-13, AC-14

  server.test.ts        # AC-17
  galaxy.test.ts        # AC-1
  smoke.test.ts         # AC-20, AC-21, AC-22

## 15. D3 Priority Rationale

All ACs are assigned `blocker` criticality by default unless there is a clear architectural argument for degradation:

- **blocker** (17 ACs): Core gameplay mechanics (navigation, trading, travel, combat, upgrades, save/load) and hard constraints (offline, one-command startup). Without these, the game is not playable or violates explicit constraints.
- **degradable** (4 ACs): Flee from combat (AC-12), HUD display (AC-18), Elite rating progression (AC-19), 60 FPS rendering (AC-20). The game remains playable without these: combat can be fight-only, status can be inferred without HUD overlay, rating is a progression metric, and lower framerates are tolerable.
- **nice_to_have** (2 ACs): Health endpoint (AC-17) is a factory verification tool, not gameplay. English-only text (AC-23) is a cosmetic quality attribute verified by inspection.

## 16. D4 Decomposition Pattern per Module Cluster

| Cluster | Modules | Pattern | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Navigation | galaxy | A (single-module) | Galaxy data and map rendering are co-located; no cross-module coordination needed |
| Economy | trading, upgrades | A (per-module) | Buy/sell and upgrades are independent trading operations sharing game-state reads |
| Travel | travel, combat | B (cross-module) | Jump execution triggers encounter checks and combat state transitions |
| Persistence | save-load, game-state | B (cross-module) | Save/load serializes the full game-state surface; new-game creation is a game-state factory |
| Server | server | A (single-module) | Thin static file server with one endpoint; no dependency on client modules |
| Presentation | rendering, ui, rating | A (per-module) | Rendering reads game-state; rating is a pure calculation; UI manages screen routing |
